items.question: What would happen if consciousness were cut off from all things?
premises: Consciousness is by nature awareness itself
If consciousness were cut off from all things it would become a mere object
A mere object would be like a pot defined only by its own mark
items.inference: Consciousness cannot be cut off from all things without ceasing to be consciousness.
items.plain_english: If consciousness, whose nature is awareness, were cut off from all things, it would become a mere object, like a pot defined only by its own particular mark.

items.question: What follows if consciousness is sought to be cut off?
premises: Cutting consciousness off from things means loss of its nature as consciousness
If consciousness loses its nature as consciousness it perishes
Consciousness flees away if one tries to divide it
items.inference: Any attempt to cut consciousness off destroys consciousness itself.
items.plain_english: Therefore, from the loss of its nature as consciousness, this consciousness perishes; for if one seeks to cut consciousness off, it flees away.

rows.grounds: compound with iva: nija-uttamāṅga-cchāyā + iva; sandhi noted in grounds

items.question: Why does the ordinary person not see all things in the divine?
premises: All things are declared to exist in the divine
The ordinary person does not see all things in the divine
This is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head
items.inference: The ordinary person fails to see all in the divine because it is inseparably close, like one's own shadow.
items.plain_english: And the fact that the great mass of people does not see all things in me, though it has been declared so, is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head while walking.

items.question: Why is the ordinary person established in the divine yet unaware of it?
premises: The ordinary person abides in the midst of all and is established in the divine
He is not grounded in the light of awareness
He treats the divine presence as if it were unreal
items.inference: Being established in the divine does not guarantee recognition when one lacks grounding in light.
items.plain_english: Because he abides in the midst of all, he is indeed established in me; yet, because he is not grounded in the light and treats it as unreal, he does not recognize this.

items.question: What did the sage declare by following both paths?
premises: The sage declared destruction by both paths of reasoning
This is the order of reality described so far
This order is called the enclosure or mutual containment
items.inference: The sage's twofold teaching establishes the principle of mutual enclosure as the order of reality.
items.plain_english: The sage declared that this amounts to destruction by both paths; this, so far, is the order of reality which is called the enclosure.

items.question: How does consciousness relate to the seat containing all paths?
premises: From that very enclosure arises the seat containing all paths
Consciousness attains the state of being supported in that abode
Consciousness again attains the state of being the support
items.inference: Consciousness alternately appears as supported and as support within the seat of all paths.
items.plain_english: From that very principle, in the abode of the seat that contains all the paths, consciousness attains the state of being supported and again becomes the support.

rows.grounds: desiderative participle of pra-viś, genitive plural

items.question: Why does the sage speak again of the seat in this context?
premises: The seat was already spoken of in the supreme worship
Here the sage speaks again for those wishing to enter
He does so according to the order of cognition
items.inference: The sage restates the teaching of the seat to guide aspirants according to their cognitive progression.
uncertainties: The spacing marker \hspace{3cm} is editorial and not a lexical token.
items.plain_english: And in the supreme worship the seat was spoken of again; therefore here, for those wishing to enter, the sage speaks according to the order of cognition.

items.question: Why does the Lord declare the universe to be nothing other than himself?
premises: The Lord has spoken that the universe is not otherwise than himself
The freedom of undivided consciousness shines forth on the path of difference
What appears as difference is the expression of that same freedom
items.inference: The universe is identical with the Lord because undivided consciousness freely appears as difference.
items.plain_english: The Lord has indeed declared that the universe is not other than that, because the freedom of undivided consciousness shines forth on the path of difference.

items.question: How is the distinction between teacher and taught established?
premises: The arrangement of taught and teacher is extended on the path of difference
One's own self is regarded as the teacher
That same self is regarded as the supreme god
items.inference: The roles of teacher and taught are projections of the one self appearing as distinct.
items.plain_english: This arrangement of the one to be taught and the teacher is extended; for one's own self is regarded as the teacher and as the supreme god.

items.question: How does the self misrecognize its own expressions in the state of difference?
premises: One considers self-uttered statements as spoken by another
The thing to be taught and the means by which it is taught appear distinct
These distinctions arise within the same self
items.inference: In the differentiated state, the self attributes its own expressions and teachings to an other.
items.plain_english: One considers statements uttered by oneself as spoken by another; and the thing to be taught and that by which it is taught are likewise taken as distinct.

items.question: How is the differentiated teaching comparable to a dream?
premises: All of this is in reality of the nature of the self
Yet one regards it only through difference
This is like experiencing a lineage of instruction in a dream state
items.inference: Differentiated teaching is a self-created appearance, analogous to instruction occurring within a dream.
items.plain_english: Indeed all that is of the nature of the self, yet one regards it as different, just as one experiences a lineage of instruction while situated in the dream state.

rows.grounds: present participle of ā-karṇaya with sandhi before jaḍo

items.question: How is waking experience similar to a dream experience?
premises: In a dream a dull creature hears and takes what is self-produced as spoken by another
The entire waking world of ordinary activity is contained within waking consciousness
The same misattribution occurs in waking as in dream
items.inference: Waking conventional activity is structurally analogous to dream, since both involve taking the self's display as other.
items.plain_english: Just as a dull creature in a dream hears and regards what is spoken as coming from another, so too this entire ordinary activity contained within waking is regarded in the same way.

items.question: What difference remains between dream and waking on this view?
premises: An objection asks what difference there would then be between dream and waking
The answer will be given later
Alternatively, for the free Lord nothing is impossible to express
items.inference: The apparent objection does not limit the free Lord, whose expression can encompass both dream and waking.
items.plain_english: If one asks what difference there would then be between dream and waking, that will be explained later; or else, what has not been spoken by the free Lord?

items.question: What is the real basis of the distinction between injunction and restatement?
premises: The difference between injunction and restatement arises only by the order of cognition
One may say all is God or God is all
In reality these are one and the same
items.inference: Injunction and restatement differ only in cognitive sequence, not in the underlying reality.
items.plain_english: Thus the difference between injunction and restatement exists only by the order of cognition; whether one says 'all is God' or 'God is all', it is indeed one and the same.

rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun with sandhi before chrī
aorist of abhi-dhā with elided a

items.question: How did Narayana express the identity of God and the universe?
premises: In reality the universe is like jar and pot, a matter of mere synonymy
The difference is only in what is to be expressed
Glorious Narayana declared to them 'you indeed are that'
items.inference: The scriptural identity statement rests on the real non-difference of God and the universe.
items.plain_english: In reality the universe is a matter of mere synonymy, like 'jar' and 'pot'; what differs is only the expression. Therefore glorious Narayana declared to them, 'You indeed are that.'

rows.grounds: objection particle with sandhi before abhede

items.question: How can injunction and restatement operate if there is no difference?
premises: An objection asks how injunction and restatement are possible in non-difference
The example given is 'this toothy one is Caitra'
In that example the toothy one is first restated
items.inference: The objection challenges whether logical roles of restatement and injunction can arise without real difference.
items.plain_english: But surely, if there is non-difference, how can there be an arrangement of injunction and restatement? For example, 'this toothy one is Caitra' first restates the toothy one.

rows.grounds: proper name in vocative-like citation form
ablative of caitra with sandhi before caitraś
proper name with sandhi before cānyas

items.question: What absurdity follows if restatement and injunction imply real difference?
premises: If after restating the toothy one the part 'Caitra' is enjoined as different
Then the toothy one would be other than Caitra
And Caitra would be other than the toothy one
items.inference: Treating injunction and restatement as requiring real difference leads to an impossible split of one referent.
items.plain_english: If, after restating him, the part 'Caitra' is enjoined as something else, then the toothy one would be other than Caitra and Caitra other than the toothy one; how could that be?

rows.grounds: relative pronoun with sandhi before eva

items.question: What is the correct relation between the restated and enjoined terms?
premises: A case like 'the pot is Caitra' would not count as injunction and restatement
Injunction and restatement require identity of referent
Therefore the one who is Caitra is the same as the toothy one
items.inference: Injunction and restatement operate on one and the same referent, not on different entities.
items.plain_english: A case like 'the pot is Caitra' would not be injunction and restatement; therefore the situation is that the very one who is Caitra is the toothy one.

items.question: When are injunction and restatement legitimately used?
premises: The distinction of injunction and restatement is real in use but arises only from cognition
It is employed for those who do not yet know synonymous terms
Examples include tree and earth-grower, jar and pot, and the statement that the Great Lord is all this world
items.inference: Injunction and restatement serve to reveal identity to those who have not yet recognized synonymous expressions of the same reality.
items.plain_english: The distinction between injunction and restatement is real in practice but arises only from cognition; it is used for those who do not yet know synonymous terms, as in 'this is a tree, an earth-grower' or 'a jar, a pot', and likewise in saying 'the Great Lord is all this world.'

rows.grounds: compound: saṃhāra-sṛṣṭi-aṃśa-śata, neuter plural with sandhi
compound: antaḥ-sthita, neuter plural with sandhi

items.question: What is the nature of the state established by the union of enclosure?
premises: By the union of enclosure a certain state is established
That state is perfectly full
Within it stand hundreds of phases of dissolution and creation
items.inference: The state of mutual enclosure is a plenitude that internally contains countless cycles of creation and dissolution.
items.plain_english: In this way, by the union of enclosure, there is indeed a perfectly full state in which even hundreds of phases of dissolution and creation stand within.

rows.grounds: compound: upāsitum-manas with sandhi before tayā

items.question: How do some practitioners approach that plenary state?
premises: Some are minded to worship that plenary state part by part
They approach it through divisions arising as one, doubled, four, six, twelve, and so on
These divisions are modes of engaging the same state
items.inference: Practitioners approach the one plenary consciousness through graduated numerical differentiations.
items.plain_english: Some, wishing to worship that very state part by part, do so through divisions arising as one, twofold, four, six, twelve, and so forth.

items.question: How is the one consciousness differentiated into multiple forms?
premises: Consciousness is divided by various sequences into wheels of consciousness
The one consciousness becomes twofold as knowing and acting
That same consciousness then becomes threefold
items.inference: The divisions of practice are structured unfoldings of the one consciousness into functional modes.
items.plain_english: By various sequences it divides itself through distinctions made of wheels of consciousness: the one consciousness becomes twofold as knowing and acting, and then that same consciousness becomes threefold.

rows.grounds: compound ablative: pronmeṣa-śakti-sācivya with sandhi before caturdhāpy

items.question: How do the fourfold and fivefold divisions of consciousness arise?
premises: With the assistance of the unfolding power consciousness is also spoken of as fourfold
Through ascent in the bliss of the power of consciousness it is declared fivefold
These are further articulations of the same consciousness
items.inference: The fourfold and fivefold forms arise from the same consciousness through unfolding and blissful ascent.
items.plain_english: Then, through the assistance of the unfolding power, it is also spoken of as fourfold; and through ascent in the bliss of the power of consciousness, this same consciousness is declared to be fivefold.

items.question: How far do the numerical differentiations of consciousness extend?
premises: Consciousness is contemplated as sixfold through the worship taught as the six vowels
It extends up to a twelvefold form
These forms apply in the creation of consciousness and in domains of equal scope
items.inference: The one consciousness unfolds into multiple ordered forms, from sixfold to twelvefold, within the same field of manifestation.
items.plain_english: It is sixfold through contemplation of the worship of consciousness taught as the six vowels, and extends up to twelvefold in the creation of consciousness and in domains of equal scope.
